Fractions on a Number Line: Hands-On Activities + FREE Printables

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:41
Instaread

Teaching fractions on a number line? Get your students up and moving with this hands-on fraction activity!

Instead of practicing only on worksheets, students work together to create a large number line, plot fractions, and explain their thinking.

This activity helps students visualize fractions as numbers, recognize equivalent fractions, and understand fractions greater than 1.

Get Up and Move! Fractions on a Number Line

One of my favorite ways to help students understand fractions is to make the number line BIG!

All you need is some bulletin board paper, tape, or string and the FREE printable fraction cards.

Here’s how to set it up:

  1. Create a large number line. Use bulletin board paper, tape, or string to make a number line on the floor, wall, or table.
  2. Partition the number line. Have students identify the whole numbers and divide the intervals into equal parts.
  3. Plot the fractions. Students work together to place the fraction cards in the correct locations.
  4. Record their work. Students draw and label their completed number lines on the recording sheets.

Build Fraction Understanding Through Discussion

As students place their fraction cards, encourage them to explain how they know where each fraction belongs.

For example, when working with fourths, students might discover that 2/4 and 1/2 belong at the same point on the number line.

They can also see that 4/4 is equal to 1 and that fractions such as 6/4 extend beyond one whole.

This is a great opportunity to ask:

• How many equal parts are between 0 and 1?
• Why do 2/4 and 1/2 belong at the same location?
• How can a fraction be greater than 1?
• What do you notice about the numerator and denominator when a fraction equals 1?

These conversations help students connect fraction notation to visual models.

What’s Included in the FREE Fraction Activity?

I’ve included 5 printable fraction number line activities that you can use with small groups or during whole-class instruction.

• Activity 1: Halves and fourths
• Activity 2: Thirds
• Activity 3: Halves and sixths
• Activity 4: Fourths, halves, and fractions greater than 1
• Activity 5: Sixths, halves, and fractions greater than 1

Each activity includes printable fraction cards and a recording sheet. A one-page answer key with completed number lines is also included!
